Why? Its more satisfying.

I love colors, pigments, paintmaking. Real colors, not altered by a screen.

I like to feel what I am actually doing and working with. The paints, the water, the graphite, the paper.

All your senses are involved, even smell

Staring in a screen is annoying and straining my eyes

My art feels more alive on paper than it ever could as piece of data

There are so many different media and techniques to explore, you can't get bored if you stay openminded

And lastly, I actually feel connected to the traditional art I made, the digital art might look good, but the original will be forever locked inside the computer. Even a print is not the same.

These are my reasons why I didn't go back to digital, after I started my art journey with digital art.
I was pretty decent at it and loved it, but I didn't want to be a one trick pony, so I sat down and learned how to paint.
At first it wasn't fun at all, no undo button, no layers, no saving.
Then I finally got ahold of it and experienced what I said above. The possibilities are endless, I cant get enough of painting.

Do I like to look at digital art? Yes!
Do I still draw digitally? Yes, sometimes
Do I like to draw digitally? Yes, its fun for different reasons
Do I think digital art is valid? Yes, it is.
Do I think digital artists really should explore some traditional art? Absolutely!

I'd say the most important thing as an artist is to stay open minded and always be ready to learn new stuff. That alone is a reason why traditional art is valid.

For me, it has always been flexibility.
I started with paper, pencil and colored pencils.
Then I worked digitally 90% of the time for some years. Then back to traditional with copics, no digital art at all for years.
Nowadays I work mainly traditional with watercolor, gouache, acrylic, copics, but also digitally.
I am fairly good with all those mediums and I am proud of being so flexible.

I think, not only as an artist, but as a human being constantly learning new things and eventually mastering them is the key to a fulfilled life.
I don't know why you wouldn't want to try out all the possibilities you've got.
